And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said 21st century India is moving forward with principles
of pro-people, pro-active and good governance.
The Prime Minister said the country is moving rapidly on the reform express and the
institutions that conduct examinations must also work on reforms that are the need
of the country.
addressing the centenary celebrations of Union Public Service Commission UPSC at
Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today the Prime Minister stressed on the need to
bring young people into public services who are drawn not to public office but
to public service.
The
Prime Minister said an examination should not be considered just an event as it is related
to the future of the youth.
Mr Modi noted that a delay of even a few months can create difficulties for the youth
and, therefore, the examination system should follow the principle of time-certainty.
President Dharupati Murmur vice-president S. P. Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra
Modi have praised Captain Smith-Machar for his heroic courage in preventing a major
tragedy and saving many precious lives.
Israeli Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump have also
hailed Smith-Machar as a hero who averted a brig tragedy.
Mr. Netanyahu thanked Captain Smith Machhar for saving the lives of 174 people on board
Tel Aviv-bound flight Dubai flight.
Prime Minister Modi said, Captain Smith is a hero, and India is proud of him.
Prime Minister Modi also spoke to the wife and parents of Captain Smith Machar.
The ambassador of India to the UAE, Deepak Mittal met Captain Smith Machar's family
in Dubai.
He informed our West Asia correspondent that Captain Smith has been flown to UAE for
treatment and his condition is stable.
The brave son of India, Captain Smith, has done really wonders, a great service to the
humanity.
He led with an example and saved so many precious lives and our tragedy.
I met him along with his family here in the hospital in UAE.
I was very relieved and very reassured, I would say, that he is doing well, he is
quite stable.
He was talking, he was chatting, bit of discomfort, but I think he is under good
medical care here in UAE.
Meanwhile, special prayers are being offered across major pilgrimage sites in Gujarat
for the speedy recovery and long life of Flight Dubai Captain Smith-Macher, a report.
Special prayers and continuous Vedic chants are underway at the holy shrines of Somnath and Ambaji
for the quick recovery of Braveheart Captain Smith-Macher who is originally from Gujarat.
Special prayers were offered at the Chanchar Chowk of Ambaji Temple
while an uninterrupted Mahamrithinjay Mantraja and Mahapuja began at Somnath Chotirling.
Joining the nation in praying for the captain, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patil
praised his selfless weller and announced the prestigious Vishishtha Gujarat Garima Award
to honour his heroic actions.
Aparna Khunt, Aakashwari News, Ahmedabad.
Union Home Affairs Minister Amit Shah today chaired a meeting in New Delhi to resolve the
long-standing Mahanadi water dispute.
Union Jal Shakti Minister Siyar Patil, the chief ministers of Chhattisgarh and Odisha,
and other senior officials were present at the meeting.
The dispute over sharing of Mahanadi waters between Chhattisgarh and Udisha has remained
unresolved for several years.
Udisha had requested the central government in November 2016 to set up a tribunal to resolve
the dispute after talks failed to resolve the issue.
The Mahanadi water disputes tribunal was constituted in March 2018.
Government has extended the validity of exempted fast tags from existing one year to up
to five years for Divyangjan, depending on the degree of disability. The Centre has revised
the guidelines for issuance and renewal of the exempted fast tags for eligible Divyangjan
and persons with disability beneficiaries. The guidelines will come into effect from
tomorrow. More in this report.
The revised provisions are aimed at making the National Highway Tolling Ecosystem
more accessible, transparent and user-friendly for eligible Divyangjan. Under the guidelines,
designs vehicles specially designed and constructed for use by persons with physical disabilities
as well as vehicles registered under the ownership type, the Vyang Zhen will be issued Exempted
Fast Tag. It will be based on the percentage of disability recorded in a valid disability
certificate, unique disability identity card or other applicable records. The revised
framework is also aimed at bringing greater uniformity in the issuance and renewal
of exempted fast-tags for eligible deviantian and PWD vehicles while reducing the need for
repeated procedural formalities.
With Suparna Sekya, Rishu Jaiswal, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The government has extended the last date for submission of applications under the National
Means Come Merit Scholarship Scheme until the 31st of this month.
The Ministry of Education said, the extension will provide eligible students additional
time to complete their applications on the National Scholarship Portal and facilitate
timely verification by the concerned authorities.
Eight students drowned at Deviagar Beach in Raigar district of Maharashtra today.
Police said all eight bodies have been recovered.
The students were part of a group of 42 students from a private coaching class in
Alandipune district.
Some of the students were studying in class 11 while others were in class 12.
itself.
Police said some students from the group went swimming at the beach, located around 170
km from Mumbai.
Eight of them could not return to the shore.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Welcome back.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Deshseva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the government has been ceaselessly working towards
achieving the goal of a wixit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social
empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. In this special series, today we
We bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through the
establishment of monuments like the National War Memorial and National Police Memorial.
The National War Memorial was established in January 2019.
The monument, built near India Gate, is dedicated to honouring soldiers of the Indian Armed
Forces who made supreme sacrifice in conflicts after independence.
Apart from the main memorial, there is a dedicated area for busts of 21 soldiers
soldiers who have been comforted with the nation's highest-gallantry award in war, Paravir Chakra.
In his month's program on Akashwani in 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had said that
the memorial symbolizes the spirit of valor of the country's brave soldiers.
Delhi's heart, that is the place where India Gate and Amar Jawan Jyoti are present.
Just close to that, a new path has been made.
The National Science Path, after independence, is the path of the youth,
the path of nationalism.
The identity of the National Science Path will be formed in such a place,
where people will take information about the great martyrs of the country,
Talking to Akashwani News, a student from Delhi University, Tufail shared that his experience
at the National War Memorial has been incredible.
My experience at the National War Memorial has been such a fantastic experience.
The entire idea of depicting the names of all martyrs of this nation, all the soldiers
who sacrificed their life for this nation, it's such a great idea.
It is a reminder of constant sacrifices that we have to make in order to protect our nation
from our enemies.
And at the same time, it's also surrounded with flora and fauna and it's such a huge
place and I would suggest everybody should visit this place once."
The Prime Minister also dedicated to the country the National Police Memorial in 2018 on the
occasion of Police Commemoration Day.
More than monuments, these establishments pay tribute to the men and women in uniform
who guard the country, combat terrorism and crime, maintain law and order, and rush to
aid during disasters and emergencies.
with Priya Mondal, Banu Pratap Singh Akashwani, News Daily.
The United States has imposed sanctions on 10 individuals and entities across several countries
for allegedly helping procure weapons and military components for Iran's Ministry of
Defense and Armed Forces logistics.
In a report, the media line says that among those sanctioned is a Pakistani businessman
along with three companies linked to the person.
More over, the businessman is chairman of the Pakistan-based Cavalier Group, a private
defense company with operations in Pakistan and other countries.
Bihar continues to battle floods.
Several rivers in the state are flowing above the danger mark, more from our correspondent.
Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary has sought the assistance of the Indian Air Force for
relief and rescue operations in view of the seriousness of the situation.
After inspecting the rising water level of the Ganga in Patna today, Mr Chaudhary
told reporters that the next 48 hours will be extremely crucial for Bihar.
Amid the rising water level of the Gandak, breaches in embankments at several places
have led to the rapid spread of floodwater in low-lying areas.
Saran, Gopalganj, Ischamparan, Vischamparan and Visali are among the worst affected districts.
The rising water levels of the Bhagmati and Kosi have also inundated several villages
businesses in Darbhanga, Samastipur, Supol and Sahar Shah districts, Aseez Ranjan for
Aakashwani News, Patna.
India Meteorological Department or IMD has forecast heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh
tomorrow.
IMD said conditions are likely to become favorable for further withdrawal of southwest
monsoon from remaining parts of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Taya
Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand during next 48 hours.
as the MED department predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds
over southern states, Orisha, sub-Himalian West Bengal and parts of northeast tomorrow.
On to sports. At the Asian Games 2026 in Japan, India enjoyed another action-packed
day-to-day with the men's hockey and cricket teams reaching their respective finals. Men's
hockey team defeated their arch-rivals Pakistan 4-3 in a thrilling semi-final, while the
The cricket team beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs to book a place in the gold medal match.
Greco-Roman wrestler Nitesh Sivach today bagged silver medal in men's 97kg at Asian Games in Japan.
Nitesh lost to Japan's Yuri Nakazato 04 in the final.
Indian pair of Manu Francis and Princess Kuri Sinkal Noble bagged the silver medal in the men's
skiff opening race 9 of the Asian Games Sailing Competition.
It is India's first sailing medal of the Asian Games.
The team of Harshitha Tomar and Sheetal Varma won the bronze medal in the Women's Kif Sailing
event.
Ganesh Mani Ratnam Tirumuru got bronze in the individual compound archery.
India's medal tally has risen to 66 including 10 gold, 23 silver and 33 bronze medals.
